fix(phonesync): answer a relayed marks ask from what the engine had at the ask

## Summary

Flaky in CI on macOS and Windows; the cause is in the app.

Through the storage relay a phone's ask for a film's word marks did not wait: it raced a zero timer against the run's done channel. When the run finished before that select, both cases were ready and Go picks one at random, so the same ask answered pending or the computed marks by chance, which made TestPluginMarksForAPhone flaky on macOS and Windows. A relayed ask now answers pending whenever the marks were still being computed when the engine looked, and the phone asks again.


## Tests

`go test -count=30 -run TestPluginMarksForAPhone` passes.

## Screenshots

None (no visual change).

fix(store): a clean close clears the lock's pid, so a standby takes over

Fixes #3975

## What

A clean close of the authority store now empties the pid payload of `authority.lock` while it still holds the OS lock, then unlocks. A standby that takes over while the old GameWorld is still exiting opens the store instead of refusing it.

## Why

r203 reverted twice on 2026-11-20. Each time the standby took over about 80 ms after the old GameWorld's `shutdown: complete`, read the old pid from the payload, found that process still alive (it exited about 70 ms later), and died with `authority store is locked by live pid`. The full timeline is in #3975.

## Change

`internal/data/store`:

| Function | Change |
|---|---|
| `releaseLock` (new) | The one clean release of an `acquireLock` handle: empty the payload under the OS lock, unlock, close. |
| `releaseClaimFunc` (`Store.Close`) | Uses `releaseLock` instead of its own unlock and close. |
| `InitializeAuthority` | The same. |

Not changed:
- A killed owner still leaves its payload, which the dead-pid rule reclaims as before.
- An owner that has not closed still refuses a second writer, by the OS lock.
- `acquireLock`'s refusal path leaves another process's payload untouched.

Every unlock of the lock (`rg "unlockFileExclusive\(|releaseLock\("`) is now `releaseLock` or that refusal path. No other code reads the payload (`rg "lockFilePayload|LockFileName"` outside `lockfile.go` finds only `InitializeAuthority`'s acquire).

## Tests

`lockfile_handover_test.go` runs a real second process, the test binary itself:
- `TestLockOpensAfterLiveOwnerClosedCleanly`: the helper opens and closes the store and stays alive, and the next `Open` must succeed. Before the fix it failed with the production message: `authority store is locked by live pid 50672 ... a second writer would corrupt`.
- `TestLockRefusesWhileLiveOwnerHoldsIt`: a helper that holds the store open still refuses a second writer.

Ran:
- `go test ./internal/data/store -count=1` on Windows: ok (114.5 s, with the PC loaded).
- The lock tests on Linux (`golang:1.27.4`): all 11 pass, including both new ones.
- `pnpm task check:server:changed`: build, gofmt, vet, golangci-lint and race passed. The tests step failed only on the 30 s per-package time budget: the store package took 40.4 s alone, and it is over the budget on this PC without the change too. Timed alone with the new tests skipped:

  | Run | Without the payload clear | With it |
  |---|---|---|
  | 1 | 84.2 s | 49.5 s |
  | 2 | 53.4 s | 46.1 s |

  CI's runner judges the budget.

Native trace: none. Process locking is port-only infrastructure, with no game behaviour.

diff --git a/apps/server/internal/data/store/lockfile_handover_test.go b/apps/server/internal/data/store/lockfile_handover_test.go
new file mode 100644
index 000000000..a94cad11c
--- /dev/null
+++ b/apps/server/internal/data/store/lockfile_handover_test.go
@@ -0,0 +1,157 @@
+/*
+===========================================================================
+
+lockfile_handover_test.go - the store lock across a process handover
+
+The canary standby handover (opensro-ops#281) opens the authority store
+the moment the old GameWorld releases its guard, while the old process
+is still exiting. These tests run a real second process: the helper
+opens and closes the store, then stays alive, exactly like the old
+GameWorld between "shutdown: complete" and its exit.
+
+===========================================================================
+*/
+
+package store
+
+import (
+	"bufio"
+	"os"
+	"os/exec"
+	"path/filepath"
+	"strings"
+	"testing"
+)
+
+const (
+	envLockHandoverHelper = "SRO_LOCK_HANDOVER_HELPER"
+	envLockHandoverDir    = "SRO_LOCK_HANDOVER_DIR"
+	envLockHandoverClose  = "SRO_LOCK_HANDOVER_CLOSE"
+	lockHandoverReady     = "store-ready"
+)
+
+/*
+================
+startLockHandoverHelper
+
+Run this test binary as a second process that opens the store in dir,
+closes it when closeStore is set, prints lockHandoverReady and then
+lives until the returned release function closes its stdin.
+================
+*/
+func startLockHandoverHelper(t *testing.T, dir string, closeStore bool) func() {
+	t.Helper()
+	command := exec.Command(os.Args[0], "-test.run=^TestLockHandoverHelperProcess$")
+	closeValue := "0"
+	if closeStore {
+		closeValue = "1"
+	}
+	command.Env = append(os.Environ(),
+		envLockHandoverHelper+"=1",
+		envLockHandoverDir+"="+dir,
+		envLockHandoverClose+"="+closeValue,
+	)
+	stdin, err := command.StdinPipe()
+	if err != nil {
+		t.Fatalf("helper stdin: %v", err)
+	}
+	stdout, err := command.StdoutPipe()
+	if err != nil {
+		t.Fatalf("helper stdout: %v", err)
+	}
+	if err := command.Start(); err != nil {
+		t.Fatalf("start helper: %v", err)
+	}
+	release := func() {
+		_ = stdin.Close()
+		_ = command.Wait()
+	}
+	lines := bufio.NewScanner(stdout)
+	for lines.Scan() {
+		if strings.TrimSpace(lines.Text()) == lockHandoverReady {
+			// Drain the rest so the helper never blocks on a full pipe.
+			go func() {
+				for lines.Scan() {
+				}
+			}()
+			return release
+		}
+	}
+	release()
+	t.Fatalf("helper exited before it opened the store")
+	return nil
+}
+
+/*
+================
+TestLockHandoverHelperProcess
+
+The helper body; a no-op unless startLockHandoverHelper launched it.
+================
+*/
+func TestLockHandoverHelperProcess(t *testing.T) {
+	if os.Getenv(envLockHandoverHelper) != "1" {
+		return
+	}
+	s, err := Open(os.Getenv(envLockHandoverDir), Options{})
+	if err != nil {
+		os.Stderr.WriteString("helper open: " + err.Error() + "\n")
+		os.Exit(2)
+	}
+	if os.Getenv(envLockHandoverClose) == "1" {
+		s.Close()
+	}
+	os.Stdout.WriteString(lockHandoverReady + "\n")
+	// Alive until the parent releases us: the exiting old GameWorld.
+	buffer := make([]byte, 1)
+	for {
+		if _, err := os.Stdin.Read(buffer); err != nil {
+			break
+		}
+	}
+	os.Exit(0)
+}
+
+/*
+================
+TestLockOpensAfterLiveOwnerClosedCleanly
+
+2026-11-20 r203: the standby took over 83 ms after the old GameWorld's
+"shutdown: complete" and refused with "locked by live pid": the old
+process had dropped the OS lock but left its pid in the payload, and it
+was still alive. A clean Close is a release, so the next opener must
+get the store while the closed owner lives on.
+================
+*/
+func TestLockOpensAfterLiveOwnerClosedCleanly(t *testing.T) {
+	dir := t.TempDir()
+	release := startLockHandoverHelper(t, dir, true)
+	defer release()
+
+	s, err := Open(dir, Options{})
+	if err != nil {
+		t.Fatalf("a store its live owner closed cleanly must open: %v", err)
+	}
+	s.Close()
+}
+
+/*
+================
+TestLockRefusesWhileLiveOwnerHoldsIt
+
+The other side of the handover: an owner that has NOT closed still
+refuses a second process, by the OS lock.
+================
+*/
+func TestLockRefusesWhileLiveOwnerHoldsIt(t *testing.T) {
+	dir := t.TempDir()
+	release := startLockHandoverHelper(t, dir, false)
+	defer release()
+
+	if _, err := Open(dir, Options{}); err == nil {
+		t.Fatal("a store held by a live process must refuse a second writer")
+	}
+	if _, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(dir, LockFileName)); err != nil {
+		t.Fatalf("the held lock file must stay: %v", err)
+	}
+}

Fix targeted acceptance retry stalling on failures of unselected checks

## Problem

`accept_checks` in `dev/release-publication.py` decided whether its first (local) pass had failed by reading the receipt-wide `result`, which is `"failed"` whenever any check in the receipt failed. A targeted retry or accept of a hosted lane A therefore printed "a local check failed", returned 1 and never ran A's local fallback if some unselected check B had failed. B could be a local check or another hosted lane.

## Change

- The first pass now counts failures only among the checks it ran:
  - Targeted: the selection plus required checks, minus hosted checks.
  - Untargeted: all checks except the open hosted ones.
- An untargeted accept whose own local check failed still returns 1 without waiting for hosted jobs, as before.
- The exit code of accept still comes from the receipt-wide result, so a receipt with any failed check never returns 0.

## Tests

- New `HostedChecks.test_targeted_accept_falls_back_despite_a_failure_of_an_unselected_check` in `tests/release-publication.sh`. It covers B as a failed local check and B as a second open hosted lane. It asserts that the hosted job is awaited, then A runs locally.
- The existing untargeted-failure test now fails a real check in the receipt instead of patching the receipt result, so it exercises the per-check logic.
- The fake `run_checks` in `tests/release-acceptance-preflight.sh` now records the failed check in the receipt as well as the overall result.

Checks run: `tests/release-publication.sh`, `tests/release-acceptance.sh`, `tests/release-acceptance-preflight.sh` and `make lint` pass.

### Statistics

Computed for `619e109e1befc3e75221814bb1cfe9b685f5c837`.

| Area | Added | Removed | Purpose |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| tests | 23 | 4 | targeted retry with an unselected failed check, real per-check failures in fakes |
| fixtures and tools | 6 | 1 | first acceptance pass counts only failures of the checks it ran |
| total | 29 | 5 | |

Review cycles: 1

Checks:
- none

fix(web): keep focus off body when a closed pop-up's opener row is gone and the filter bar is hidden

Closes #4464

## Why

With one row and no filter, the whole filter bar is hidden. If a refresh removed the row a pop-up was opened from, closing the pop-up found nothing drawn to return focus to (the opener is gone, the Title box and Filters button are hidden, and so is every control in the bar), so focus fell to `body`. A keyboard or screen-reader user lost their place.

## What

`onClose` in `PullRequestDetailsDialog.svelte` gets one more candidate at the end of its list: the first drawn row title button (`#pr-rows` or `#issue-rows`). Opener, fallback and filter bar still win when they are drawn, so nothing else moves. The pull requests page gets the same candidate, since it shares the dialog. I left the per-page candidates refactor (#4418) alone.

`docs/issues.md` now says where focus goes when the opener row is gone.

## Tests

Journeys in `tests/dialog-chain-close-focus.spec.ts`, at 1280px and 390px:

- Issues page: open from Issue 5, follow a pill to Issue 6, a refresh leaves only Issue 6, close. Focus is on Issue 6's title (criteria 1 and 2), with axe in light and dark. It fails on a fresh build without the fix and passes with it.
- Pull requests page, same shape. This one already passed without the fix, so it pins the sibling path and doesn't prove the fix.

Criterion 3 (the filtered one-row case) is pinned by #4469. I ran that PR's spec against this branch: all 22 pass. It isn't in this diff, to avoid a collision in `playwright.config.ts`; this PR touches different files.

[Bug] Require a streamed body ceiling and align the reference value

## Purpose

Closes #6547. Two gaps in the streamed body guard:

- `streamed_body.enabled` without `max_bytes` loaded, and the handler then accumulated the request body without a bound: `checkBodySize` enforced the ceiling only when it was positive (`pkg/extproc/processor_req_body_streamed.go`) and nothing validated the field. Loading now refuses an enabled streamed body without a positive `max_bytes`.
- The reference configuration named `max_bytes: 1048576`, one order under the documented 10 MiB (`website/docs/installation/k8s/streamed-extproc.md`) and 64 times under the codec's 64 MiB body ceiling (`llmprotocol.DefaultPolicy().Limits.BodyBytes`), so a multi-megabyte turn was refused with 413 on a Router started from the shipped config. It now names 10 MiB.

## Test Plan

```bash
cd src/semantic-router && go test ./pkg/config -run TestStreamedBodyNeedsAMaxBytesWhenEnabled -count=1
```

The test refuses `enabled` without `max_bytes`, keeps `enabled` with 10 MiB loading (and carries the value into `MaxStreamedBodyBytes`), and keeps a disabled handler without `max_bytes` legal.

## Test Result

The enabled-without-`max_bytes` case fails on the previous revision (`err = <nil>, want … max_bytes`) and passes with the change. `./pkg/config` passes in full, including the maintained-config resolution tests over the updated reference value.

---

UOD-421: Extend README with task types, client options, errors and cost

Extends the Go SDK README for UOD-421. Covers the supported captcha types table, client options, error handling and polling, and the solution cost. All content is README-only.

**1. Supported captcha types table** - README.md
- replaces the previous 7 rows with the full 22-row table covering every request type of the module
- documents optional `MinScore` (0.1-0.9) on reCAPTCHA v2 Enterprise and the reCAPTCHA v3 request types
- splits the Cloudflare row so Turnstile Challenge and Waiting Room link to their own documentation pages
- documentation links use the current docs slugs from the official llms.txt index

**2. Client options** - README.md
- new Client Configuration section: `WithServiceURL`, `WithSoftID` (DefaultSoftID 58), `WithClientTimeout`, `WithHTTPClient`, `WithClientProxy`, `WithTimeoutsOverride` with a `New()` example

**3. Error handling and polling** - README.md
- new Error Handling section: the typed errors (`*APIError`, `*TimeoutError` with the `ErrTimeout` sentinel, `*ValidationError`, `*StatusError`, `*MalformedResponseError`), the per-type `req.Timeouts()` schedule and context cancellation

**4. Solution cost** - README.md
- documents `TaskResult.Cost` (USD) returned by `GetTaskResult` in ready responses

Commits:
- Extend supported captcha types table in README
- Document client options in README
- Document error handling and polling timeouts in README
- Document solution cost in README

 ---
 
+## 🐞 Error Handling
+
+`Solve` returns typed errors; match them with `errors.As` and the `ErrTimeout` sentinel with `errors.Is`:
+
+| Error | Meaning |
+| :--- | :--- |
+| `*TimeoutError` (`errors.Is(err, ErrTimeout)`) | The captcha type's maximum waiting time passed before a solution arrived. Carries `TaskID` and `Timeout`. |
+| `*APIError` | The API returned an error. Carries `Method`, `Code` and `Description` (e.g. `ZERO_BALANCE`). |
+| `*ValidationError` | The request struct failed validation. Carries `Field` and `Reason`. |
+| `*StatusError` | The API answered with a non-200 HTTP status. Carries `Method` and `Status`. |
+| `*MalformedResponseError` | The API response could not be parsed. |
+| `context.Canceled`, `context.DeadlineExceeded` | The passed `context.Context` was cancelled or timed out. |
+
+```go
+solution, err := client.Solve(ctx, req)
+if err != nil {
+	var apiErr *capmonster.APIError
+	switch {
+	case errors.Is(err, capmonster.ErrTimeout):
+		log.Println("no solution in time")
+	case errors.As(err, &apiErr):
+		log.Printf("API error: %s %s", apiErr.Code, apiErr.Description)
+	default:
+		log.Println(err)
+	}
+	return
+}
+```
+
+**Polling and timeouts.** The client polls `getTaskResult` automatically. Each request type defines its own schedule via `req.Timeouts()`: a pause before the first `getTaskResult` call (`FirstRequestDelay`), the polling interval (`RequestsInterval`) and the total waiting time (`Timeout`). Override the schedule with `WithTimeoutsOverride` and limit a single call with `context.WithTimeout`. `TaskResult.Cost` (ready responses of `GetTaskResult`) carries the price of the solved task in USD. Unsolved tasks are not charged.
+
+---

SofarSolar G3: fix 32-bit divide by zero

fixes #36455

#36427 was incomplete. sprig's `int64` parses strings via `cast.ToInt64`, which uses `strconv.ParseInt(s, 0, 0)`, so the bit size is the platform `int`. On 32-bit, `int64 "4294967296"` silently returns `0` and the following `mod` fails with `integer divide by zero`.

Float literals are passed as `float64` by text/template and converted to `int64` by sprig's `sub`/`mod`, so no `int`-sized 2^32 is involved on any platform. Rendered output is unchanged (e.g. `FFFFEC78` for 5000 W).

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

fix(autodiscovery): keep the Docker image tag filter with a versionfilter

Fix #11428 

Setting a versionfilter on a Docker autodiscovery crawler cleared the tag filter derived from the current tag, so the image variant could change. With the semver kind, haproxy:3.4.7-alpine was updated to 3.5-dev9-trixie, as semver reads "-alpine" as a prerelease.

The tag filter is now always kept, as the autodiscovery spec has no tag filter to override it. This applies to the dockercompose, dockerfile, helm, nomad, githubaction and woodpecker crawlers.

benchmarks.task_description:
fix(linux): release opened window editors when app stops

## Summary
- release display-wide editor CSS providers from opened Linux windows when their app stops
- cover an opened editor window left alive while the primary window exits

Closes #901

## Validation
- `go tool nsgo check -target linux -jobs 1`

diff --git a/CHANGELOG.md b/CHANGELOG.md
index 55c5925e4..7604b1259 100644
--- a/CHANGELOG.md
+++ b/CHANGELOG.md
@@ -9,6 +9,7 @@
 - Add `LineWidth` to `ui.ProgressRing` and ring `ui.Spinner` to set the track and arc width (#960 by @houko).
 - Fail the `tsx.Plugin` calls still waiting on a promise when `Plugin.Close` closes the plugin, after its cleanups run (#893 by @houko).
 - Keep the borders of `ui/chat`'s glass composer, `GlassPanel` and popovers on watchOS, which draws no Liquid Glass rim (#896 by @houko).
+- Close the windows a Linux app opened, and release their input editors' display-wide styles, when the app's own window stops (#901 by @houko).
 - Add `ToastContent.NoClose`, `Trailing` and `OnPress`, plus `Toasts.NoClose`, so apps can customize toast dismissal, trailing content and whole-toast presses while preserving child actions (#934 by @houko).
 - Register `url_schemes` in the iOS app and hand their links to `mobile.OnOpenLinks`, at a cold launch and while the app runs, through `scene:openURLContexts:` (#909 by @houko).
 - Let Android's system tab bar follow the app theme's surface, inactive text, active text and accent-container colors (#936 by @houko).

index aa6c224ae..e59e9c675 100644
--- a/internal/platform/linux/native_test.go
+++ b/internal/platform/linux/native_test.go
@@ -282,6 +282,35 @@ func TestWindowCloseReleasesEditorProviders(t *testing.T) {
 	waitFor("both opened windows closed", before)
 	w.onLoop(t, w.close)
 	waitFor("the app closed", before)
+	// A window the app opened that is still open when the app's own window stops goes with it, and its providers too.
+	app = core.AppRoot(func(cx *core.Scope) {
+		cx.SetShutdownMode(core.ShutdownOnExplicit)
+		cx.OpenWindow(core.WindowOptions{Title: "nsgo-editors-left", Width: 200, Height: 120}, func(*core.Scope) core.Node { return inputs() })
+	})
+	w = startTestWindow(t, app, Options{Title: "nsgo-app-left", Width: 120, Height: 80, Hidden: true})
+	waitFor("the window left open open", before+2)
+	var left *window
+	w.onLoop(t, func() {
+		windowHandles.Range(func(_, v any) bool {
+			if o := v.(*window); !o.primary && o.win != 0 && goString(gtkWindowGetTitle(o.win)) == "nsgo-editors-left" {
+				left = o
+			}
+			return true
+		})
+	})
+	if left == nil {
+		t.Fatal("the opened window was not found")
+	}
+	w.onLoop(t, w.close)
+	waitFor("the app closed with a window left open", before)
+	for deadline := time.Now().Add(10 * time.Second); ; time.Sleep(10 * time.Millisecond) {
+		if _, ok := windowHandles.Load(left.handle); !ok {
+			break
+		}
+		if time.Now().After(deadline) {
+			t.Fatal("the window left open outlived the app")
+		}
+	}
